prompt: This is an art-direction redesign for Yorimichi, a stylised Japanese autumn exploration game made in Unreal. Image 1 is a real, unretouched screenshot of the game as it is now. Repaint THE SAME VIEW from the same camera, keeping the layout, street grid, terrain, building positions, sea and sky composition, but redesigned to the standard of a polished commercial stylised game (think Ghibli-inspired, hand-crafted, cosy, dense and lived-in): textured materials with soft hand-painted detail instead of flat untextured colour, coherent warm autumn palette, gentle afternoon sunlight. It must stay a believable real-time game frame built from meshes, textures and foliage, not a loose illustration. No text, no UI, no watermark. The arrival road entering the city from the west. Today it is a huge bare untextured grey terrain slab with a grey road and empty ground. Redesign: a welcoming entrance road with a town gate or welcome sign, roadside rice paddies or vegetable fields, stone walls, a small roadside shrine, pine and maple trees, utility poles with wires, a bus stop, and the first houses with gardens. Every surface textured: asphalt with edge lines, grass and weeds, dirt, stone.
